reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports sigma and nitride precipitation at grain boundaries in a Cr-containing FCC HEA upon aging at 900–1300 K, and E2 links this to reduced mechanical properties. However, the evidence is from a different alloy (equiatomic CrNiFeCoMn) and does not address the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 composition, the as-built supersaturated state, or behavior in reducing vs. oxidizing environments, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: As-built Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA has a supersaturated FCC matrix with minimal secondary phases
Elevated temperature exposure (950–1300 K) drives Cr-rich sigma phase and nitride precipitation at grain boundaries
These grain-boundary precipitates weaken intergranular cohesion and cause embrittlement
The degradation mechanism operates in both oxidizing and reducing environments
Aging leads to increased precipitate volume fraction and a corresponding drop in ductility and fracture toughness
